content: 📌 Life on the International Space Station

Background
- The station was occupied by international teams of scientists over several months.
- Research was done on living conditions.

Early impressions
- The air smelt [ _____ ].
- The temperature was easy to adjust.
- The food had enough [ _____ ].
- [ _____ ] was efficient.

Problems
- Difficulties with air filters caused lack of [ _____ ].
- It was difficult to keep cabin objects secure.
- Systems were incompatible.
e g. there were problems when mixing [ _____ ] because of the preservatives.
- The [ _____ ] available were not always suitable for their purpose.
- It was difficult to access the [ _____ ] for equipment maintenance.

Suggested improvements
- Systems and equipment should undergo more extensive [ _____ ].
- In language training, astronauts needed practice in understanding the controller’s [ _____ ].
- There should be less emphasis on [ _____ ] and more on other issues.
transcript: [01:14] AUDIO: For my presentation, I'm going to summarize the findings of a research project on life aboard the International Space Station in the early days of its operation, its teething problems as it were. I'll start by giving a little background information. The space station crew were essentially a constantly changing team of scientists from different countries who lived on the space station for several months at a time. And they conducted a number of experiments, including some studies of living conditions in space, which is what I'm going to be looking at now.

[01:51] AUDIO: So, what was life like on board in the very confined conditions of the space station? Well, the early impressions recorded by the astronauts were very different from what people had expected. They'd expected that the air would smell stale or artificial. But the astronauts found that it was fresh.

[02:11] AUDIO: So that was one very positive finding. And although they were in such a confined space and people worried that it would get very hot, in fact, they found that it was very easy to turn the temperature up or down in order to keep it within a comfortable range. The feedback on the food was also positive. Astronauts on previous space stations had described the meals as boring.

[02:36] AUDIO: But the International Space Station meals were praised for their variety. So, that was another good piece of feedback. And something which is taken for granted today, but was a key morale booster in those days, was communication between the space station and Earth, which the astronauts said was clear and reliable. So, in the early days, it seems that the mood was overall very positive.

[03:07] AUDIO: However, after a few days, the difficulties and frustrations became clearer. Above all, the crew complained about the constant noise caused by the air filters, which used to rattle and buzz 24 hours a day, interrupting their sleep. As well as that, the astronauts complained that the Velcro fasteners, which were positioned all over the station, didn't work well. And so, a lot of the time, objects weren't secure in the cabin, but floated about.

[03:37] AUDIO: A particularly serious problem was that the systems used on the space station had been developed in a number of different countries, and they didn't always work well together. For example, it was impossible to mix the water produced from different systems, because it contained different sorts of preservatives, and these reacted together and blocked the pipes. Another problem was connected to repairs. At the best of times, these took up an inordinate amount of time on the station, and the crew complained that many of the tools that they'd been provided with weren't suitable for the jobs they had to do.

[04:17] AUDIO: So, they had to improvise, which meant that jobs took a lot longer than they needed to. Another related problem was to do with access to equipment that needed maintaining. Because the instructions on the equipment were often located in places where they were difficult to read, like on the back of equipment, it was often difficult or impossible to read them. So, having identified these problems, the researchers came up with a number of suggestions about how conditions could be improved on subsequent missions.

[04:52] AUDIO: First, it became clear that although there had been a great deal of consultation with the crews, the systems and equipment on the space station needed much more wide-ranging testing. Then, the whole issue of language training came under review. Astronauts from different countries had to be able to talk to the controllers on Earth and to understand them. Now, although they'd had extensive language training, the astronauts sometimes had problems comprehending what was said because they weren't familiar with the accent of the speaker.

[05:26] AUDIO: And this sometimes led to quite dangerous misunderstandings. Finally, and this is the point I found most surprising, the researchers felt that the designers of the space station were paying too much attention to safety rather than considering operating issues, that is, how the station could be run comfortably and smoothly. And the recommendation was to make changes here at quite a fundamental level. So, those were the main points I covered in the...

explanation.step3: ❓ Câu hỏi : The air smelt _____. 🎯 Xác định loại từ cần điền : Sau smelt cần một tính từ để mô tả mùi/độ dễ chịu của không khí (air) . ✅ Đáp án đúng : fresh ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : đoạn người nói nhắc đến early impressions và điều mọi người had expected về the air trên trạm không gian: "Well, the early impressions recorded by the astronauts were very different from what people had expected..." ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Xác định từ khóa trong câu: air , smell , stale or artificial (kỳ vọng ban đầu). explanation.step3: ❓ Câu hỏi : The food had enough _____. 🎯 Xác định loại từ cần điền : Sau cụm had enough cần một danh từ (nói về điểm mạnh/đặc điểm được khen). Nội dung thuộc phần food ⇒ dự đoán là một đặc điểm như chất lượng, hương vị, sự đa dạng ,… ✅ Đáp án đúng : variety ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : câu nói về feedback on the food và so sánh meals on previous space stations với ISS meals: "The feedback on the food was also positive." ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi, tập trung từ khóa food, enough (đang cần một đặc điểm của bữa ăn). content: 📌 Getting a job with an airline

- basic academic requirements: English and [ _____ ]

Training will include
- what to do in case of [ _____ ] during a flight

Application

- can download application form from website

dealing with questions from supermarket customersworking in a [ _____ ] (voluntary work)

transcript: [02:41] Man: Hello
[02:42] Ellie: Oh, hello. This is Ellie Fisher. We were at school together.
[02:49] Man: Oh, hi Ellie. How are you? What are you doing these days?
[02:53] Ellie: Well, actually, I'm looking for a job and I was wondering about applying to an airline. You know, looking after the passengers. And I heard you're doing something like that.
[03:06] Man: Yeah, I'm working as a cabin crew attendant.
[03:09] Ellie: Right. So, what does that involve?
[03:13] Man: Well, you might have to give them the initial safety demonstration before take-off, for example. You've probably seen that when you've made a journey by air.
[03:21] Ellie: Actually, I've never flown, but I'd love to. That's why I'd like a job with an airline.
[03:29] Man: Oh, right. And during the flight, you'd also be going round to see if anyone wants to buy anything.
[03:35] Ellie: So, I'd be dealing with money.
[03:37] Man: That's right. You'd be responsible for that. And then, of course, you'd be serving meals and snacks and things.
[03:44] Ellie: Okay. So, can anyone apply?

[03:46] Man: Well, there are certain requirements. You must be at least 19 years old and there's also a minimum height, that's 168 centimetres. That's to make sure you can reach the higher cupboards in the plane.
[03:59] Ellie: Right. I'm 169 centimetres, I think. What about qualifications?
[04:07] Man: You need to show that you have a good level of English, that's written and spoken, and also maths.
[04:12] Ellie: Okay. Well, I passed my exams in both those subjects, fortunately.
[04:17] Man: And it's an advantage if you can speak another language, although for cabin crew it's not essential.
[04:23] Ellie: I can speak Spanish. I did that at school until I was 16.
[04:28] Man: Excellent. That'll be very useful.
[04:31] Ellie: And I'm pretty fit. I don't have any medical problems.
[04:35] Man: Okay. Oh, and can you swim?
[04:38] Ellie: Yes.
[04:39] Man: Good, because that's another requirement. Now, if you're accepted, you'll get a six-week training course.
[05:29] Ellie: Right.

[05:30] Man: So that'll cover all aspects of the job, all the basic things you need to know, and then some special things, like what action to take if a passenger suddenly has some sort of illness while you're in the air, for example.
[05:42] Ellie: Right. I suppose you can't always count on a doctor being on board.

[05:47] Man: No. And then you'll have to do a lot of work during the training on becoming aware of the variety of cultures that your passengers may come from and the implications of that. That's really interesting, actually.
[05:58] Ellie: Okay. Well, I'd definitely like to apply. Um, what airline do you actually work for?
[06:06] Man: It's a small airline called Eurontas. That's E-U-R-O-N-T-A-S.
[06:16] Ellie: Is that N or M in the middle?
[06:19] Man: N for November. They're good people to work for. Have a look at their website. You can download the application form from there.
[06:27] Ellie: Right. I don't have much in the way of experience, though.
[06:32] AUDIO: Well, what have you done since leaving school?
[06:36] Ellie: I worked in a supermarket for a bit, on the information desk. I was helping deal with queries from customers.
[06:43] Man: Okay. Put that down. That's one of the most important aspects of the job, in fact.
[06:48] Ellie: Oh, right. And last year I also did some voluntary work as part of a team. Should I put that down, too?
[06:57] Man: Of course. That's something else they'll be looking for, being able to work with others.
[07:02] Ellie: Right.
[07:02] Man: And a lot of airlines expect you to pay for your own uniform. But the good thing about this airline is that they provide it for you.
[07:10] Ellie: Great. Well, thanks so much, Greg.

Thông tin cần nghe là chiều cao tối thiểu để ứng tuyển. ✅ Đáp án đúng : 168 ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : đoạn Greg trả lời về certain requirements (yêu cầu để ứng tuyển), đặc biệt khi nhắc tới minimum height . ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi và khoanh vùng từ khóa: at least + cm tall ⇒ chắc chắn là số đo chiều cao . Khi nghe, chú ý câu người đàn ông liệt kê yêu cầu: “You must be at least 19 years old and there’s also a minimum height , that’s 168 centimetres .” Số 19 là độ tuổi tối thiểu , còn 168 đi kèm trực tiếp với centimetres ⇒ đây là chiều cao tối thiểu cần điền. 🧐 Lưu ý : ❌ 19 => số này xuất

passages.title: Working at Parson's Fruit Farm
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "Working at Parson's Fruit Farm"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:55] AUDIO: Well, hello everyone and welcome to Parsons Fruit Farm. It's good to see a mix of so many different nationalities who have all come here on their working holidays. I'm sure you're going to enjoy working on our farm. First of all, just a few words about accommodation.

[01:13] AUDIO: I know that some of you have pitched your tents down at the campground but are looking for something more comfortable. So one option is the motel. It's located very conveniently, just a few minutes away, and they often do reduce rates if you're staying long term. And then the backpackers hostel is always very popular, though it can be busy at this time of year.

[01:35] AUDIO: Okay, so the work itself. This summer the weather's been pretty mixed. We've had a bit of everything and the forecasts have always been wrong. So some of the apples and pears aren't in great condition.

[01:50] AUDIO: That said, this season's been better than some we've had recently. And the autumn looks like it's going to be great. So we should have ideal conditions for the harvest. So, there are a number of different jobs to do.

[02:05] AUDIO: Most of you will be fruit picking. We'll give all the fruit pickers gloves to wear to protect your fingers so you won't hurt yourselves. We'll also be looking for some tractor drivers. Their job is to collect the full baskets of fruit and take them to the shed.

[02:22] AUDIO: I should say, in this country, anyone is allowed to drive a tractor on farmland once they're 13, rather than 18, as in some countries. However, we do have certain rules that are specific to our farm. You don't need to have done farm work before, but here you must have a relevant document or permit from your country that allows you to operate this type of vehicle. Then there are also lots of jobs working inside the shed.

[02:53] AUDIO: This involves sorting the fruit and cleaning it if necessary. There's a lot of heavy machinery in the shed, so when that's operating, you must wear your ear protection. The big advantage is, the shed's fully air-conditioned, so it's a pleasant environment regardless of what the weather's doing outside. Alright, well, whatever job you do, I'll just give you some final advice.

[03:18] AUDIO: When you're picking the fruit, sometimes you can break off a small branch. That's not something you need to be worried about. It'll grow back. Also, remember to have snacks and use your water bottles often.

[03:33] AUDIO: People get exhausted quickly during harvest time. And if you've got a mobile or cell, keep it with you at all times, in case there's an emergency. Alright, I'd like to quickly go over where everything is located. So look at your maps of Parsons Fruit Farm and find the main yard.
[04:34] AUDIO: It's towards the bottom of your maps. That really is the centre of the farm. Okay, the first place I'll mention is the workshop. This is close to the main yard.

[04:48] AUDIO: But you actually have to leave the yard to get into it. So you need to take the road that goes out to the orchards and you access the workshop from there. Then, the lunchroom. On the north side of the map, there's a road that curves sharply round to the left.

[05:07] AUDIO: Halfway round this bend, you'll find the entrance to the lunchroom. It's a pretty place, next to the river and also beside a little wood. You also need to be able to find the farm office. So, if you look at the main yard, you'll see there's a number of different buildings located around it.
[05:27] AUDIO: And the farm office is the smallest one. It's on the south side. Obviously, the first aid room is important. Now, this is close to the main yard, so it's quick to get there.
[05:40] AUDIO: And it's actually more or less in the middle of your maps. That little building that's attached to the farmhouse. Then the store shed. From the main yard, take the road heading north.

[05:53] AUDIO: Go past the farmhouse and turn right. The store is down that road. If you come to the vegetable gardens, you've gone too far. Now, the other thing is, the farmhouse is further than you'd expect.

Trong bài nghe, người quản lý nhắc đến lựa chọn motel và mô tả vị trí: “It’s located very conveniently, just a few minutes away” → nghĩa là rất gần nông trại / chỉ vài phút là tới . Vì vậy thông tin khớp với lựa chọn “The motel is close to the farm” → chọn B . 🧐 Lưu ý : ❌ A. The backpackers' hostel is full. => Audio chỉ nói hostel “very popular” và “can be busy at this

So some of the apples and pears aren't in great condition. That said, this season's been better than some we've had recently. And the autumn looks like it's going to be great. So we should have ideal conditions for the harvest."
explanation.step3: ❓ Câu hỏi : The weather this summer has been ✅ Đáp án đúng : C. hard to predict accurately. ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : Đoạn người nói bắt đầu nhận xét về thời tiết mùa hè và dự báo: “This summer the weather's been pretty mixed… the forecasts have always been wrong.” ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi và xác định từ khóa cần nghe: the weather this summer + mô tả đặc điểm ( has been… ). Trong audio, người nói nhấn mạnh: thời tiết “pretty mixed” (khá thất thường) và quan trọng hơn là “the forecasts have always been wrong” → dự báo liên tục sai , tức là khó dự đoán chính xác . Vì vậy, ý đúng là thời tiết mùa hè khó dự đoán → chọn C . 🧐 Lưu ý : ❌ A. perfect for growing fruit. => Audio nói thời tiết mixed và còn làm some of the apples and pears aren't
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: hard to predict accurately.

questions.prompt: The manager says that tractor drivers

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "So, there are a number of different jobs to do. Most of you will be fruit picking. We'll give all the fruit pickers gloves to wear to protect your fingers so you won't hurt yourselves. We'll also be looking for some tractor drivers. Their job is to collect the full baskets of fruit and take them to the shed. I should say, in this country, anyone is allowed to drive a tractor on farmland once they're 13, rather than 18, as in some countries. Howev"
explanation.step3: ❓ Câu hỏi : The manager says that tractor drivers ✅ Đáp án đúng : A. require an appropriate licence. ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : Đoạn người quản lý bắt đầu nói về các công việc và nhắc đến “tractor drivers”, rồi nói về quy định riêng của trang trại : “We’ll also be looking for some tractor drivers …” ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi và đoán thông tin cần nghe: “tractor drivers” + điều kiện/yêu cầu must / need / allowed (quy định dành cho người lái máy kéo). Trong bài nghe có câu chuyển ý rất quan trọng: “However, we do have certain rules …” → sau “however” thường là điều kiện thật sự cần chú ý . Người nói khẳng định: “you must have a relevant document or permit … that allows you to operate this type of vehicle” → tức là phải có giấy phép/giấy tờ
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: require an appropriate licence.

questions.prompt: Working inside the shed

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Then there are also lots of jobs working inside the shed. This involves sorting the fruit and cleaning it if necessary. There's a lot of heavy machinery in the shed, so when that's operating, you must wear your ear protection. The big advantage is, the shed's fully air-conditioned, so it's a pleasant environment regardless of what the weather's doing outside."
explanation.step3: ❓ Câu hỏi : Working inside the shed ✅ Đáp án đúng : B. can be noisy at times. ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : Đoạn người nói chuyển sang mô tả công việc “working inside the shed” và nhắc về máy móc hoạt động: “There’s a lot of heavy machinery in the shed, so when that’s operating, you must .....” ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi và dự đoán thông tin cần nghe: làm việc trong nhà kho (shed) thì có đặc điểm gì nổi bật (nhiệt độ / tiếng ồn / độ bẩn). Trong audio có cụm từ khóa “a lot of heavy machinery” và “wear your ear protection” → phải đeo bảo vệ tai nghĩa là có tiếng ồn khi máy chạy. Vì vậy “working inside the shed” đôi lúc sẽ ồn → chọn B. can be noisy at times . 🧐 Lưu ý : ❌ A. may be rather hot. => Audio nói ngược lại: “the shed’s fully air-condit
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: can be noisy at times.

questions.prompt: What final advice does the manager give?
options: Try not to damage the trees.
Leave your phones in a secure location.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Alright, well, whatever job you do, I'll just give you some final advice. When you're picking the fruit, sometimes you can break off a small branch. That's not something you need to be worried about. It'll grow back. Also, remember to have snacks and use your water bottles often. People get exhausted quickly during harvest time. And if you've got a mobile or cell, keep it with you at all times, in case there's an emergency."
explanation.step3: ❓ Câu hỏi : What final advice does the manager give? ✅ Đáp án đúng : A. Eat and drink regularly. ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : Khi người quản lý chuyển sang phần lời khuyên cuối cùng: “I’ll just give you some final advice.” ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi và xác định nhiệm vụ: nghe xem final advice (lời khuyên cuối cùng) là gì → chú ý các cụm như remember to… / keep… / don’t… Trong audio, người quản lý nhấn mạnh: “have snacks” và “use your water bottles often” → nghĩa là ăn nhẹ và uống nước thường xuyên . Vì vậy lời khuyên cuối cùng là Eat and drink regularly → chọn A . 🧐 Lưu ý : ❌ B. Try not to damage the trees. => Audio nói đôi khi “break off a small branch” nhưng “That’s not something you need to be worried about. It’ll grow back.” → không phả
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: Eat and drink regularly.

questions.prompt: [Map / Diagram Labelling] Workshop:

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Alright, I'd like to quickly go over where everything is located. So look at your maps of Parsons Fruit Farm and find the main yard. It's towards the bottom of your maps. That really is the centre of the farm. Okay, the first place I'll mention is the workshop. This is close to the main yard. But you actually have to leave the yard to get into it. So you need to take the road that goes out to the orchards and you access the workshop from there."
explanation.step3: 📌 Tìm vị trí : Workshop ✅ Đáp án đúng : G ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : Ngay sau câu “Okay, the first place I’ll mention is the workshop.” ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Trước hết, người nói yêu cầu bạn “find the main yard” và nhấn mạnh main yard là trung tâm của nông trại → đây là điểm mốc để bắt đầu dò trên bản đồ . Sau đó nghe cụm “close to the main yard” → workshop phải nằm gần Main Yard , không ở khu vực sát river hay xa về phía bắc. Điểm quyết định là: “you actually have to leave the yard… take the road that goes out to the orchards” → workshop không nằm trong Main Yard , mà phải đi ra khỏi yard và nằm trên/ở lối rẽ của con đường dẫn ‘to Orchards’ . Trên bản đồ, vị trí thỏa đúng 2 điều kiện (gần Main Yard + nằm trên đường ra Orchards) chính là G . 🧐

questions.prompt: [Map / Diagram Labelling] Lunchroom:

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Then, the lunchroom. On the north side of the map, there's a road that curves sharply round to the left. Halfway round this bend, you'll find the entrance to the lunchroom. It's a pretty place, next to the river and also beside a little wood. You also need to be able to find the farm office. So, if you look at the main yard, you'll see there's a number of different buildings located around it."
explanation.step3: 📌 Tìm vị trí : Lunchroom ✅ Đáp án đúng : B ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : Ngay sau câu “Then, the lunchroom.” ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Khi nghe thấy “On the north side of the map” , bạn phải ngước lên phía trên bản đồ để tìm khu vực đúng (vì lunchroom nằm ở phía Bắc ). Cụm “a road that curves sharply round to the left” báo hiệu bạn cần tìm đoạn đường cong gắt sang trái ở mép trên bản đồ (đặc điểm rất dễ nhận ra vì chỉ có một khúc cua lớn như vậy). Từ khóa quyết định là “Halfway round this bend” → vị trí lunchroom nằm giữa khúc cua , không phải ở đầu hay cuối đường cong. Xác nhận lại bằng mô tả cảnh quan: “next to the river” và “beside a little wood” → trên bản đồ, điểm B nằm gần river và cạnh cụm cây nhỏ ở phía trên, khớp hoàn toàn. 🧐 Lưu ý : ❌ A => D

questions.prompt: [Map / Diagram Labelling] Farm Office:

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "And the farm office is the smallest one. It's on the south side."
explanation.step3: 📌 Tìm vị trí : Farm Office ✅ Đáp án đúng : H ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : Ngay khi người nói nhắc “the farm office” và mô tả “the smallest one… on the south side” . ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Từ khóa định vị đầu tiên: “farm office” → đây là tên địa điểm cần điền trên bản đồ. Người nói không mô tả đường đi dài, mà mô tả bằng đặc điểm quanh main yard : “there’s a number of different buildings located around it” → nhìn các tòa nhà xung quanh Main Yard . Từ khóa quyết định: “the smallest one” + “on the south side” → chọn tòa nhà nhỏ nhất nằm ở phía nam của Main Yard . Trên bản đồ, vị trí thỏa đúng 2 điều kiện ( nhỏ nhất và phía nam Main Yard ) tương ứng với H . 🧐 Lưu ý : ❌ I/G => Cũng ở gần Main Yard nhưng nằm bên phải (east) , không phải south side . ❌ F

questions.prompt: [Map / Diagram Labelling] First Aid Room:

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Obviously, the first aid room is important. Now, this is close to the main yard, so it's quick to get there. And it's actually more or less in the middle of your maps. That little building that's attached to the farmhouse."
explanation.step3: 📌 Tìm vị trí : First Aid Room ✅ Đáp án đúng : F ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : Ngay sau câu “Obviously, the first aid room is important.” ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Cụm “close to the main yard” → vị trí phải gần Main Yard , nên loại các khu quá xa ở rìa bản đồ (gần river hoặc xuống tận phía dưới). Câu “more or less in the middle of your maps” → First Aid Room nằm khoảng giữa bản đồ (khu trung tâm), không phải sát sông hay sát mép dưới. Chi tiết quyết định: “That little building that’s attached to the farmhouse.” → phải là toà nhà nhỏ nằm sát/đính với Farm House . Trên bản đồ, chỉ có khu F là ô nhỏ nằm ngay cạnh Farm House (giống “building attached”) → chọn F . 🧐 Lưu ý : ❌ E => Dễ nhầm vì cũng gần Farm House , nhưng không phải “little building attached t

questions.prompt: [Map / Diagram Labelling] Store Shed:

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Then the store shed. From the main yard, take the road heading north. Go past the farmhouse and turn right. The store is down that road. If you come to the vegetable gardens, you've gone too far."
explanation.step3: 📌 Tìm vị trí : Store shed ✅ Đáp án đúng : C ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : Ngay sau câu “Then the store shed.” ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Từ main yard , nghe hướng dẫn “take the road heading north” → đi lên phía Bắc theo đường chính từ Main Yard. Tiếp theo “Go past the farmhouse and turn right.” → phải đi qua Farm House , rồi rẽ phải vào đường nhánh ngang. “The store is down that road.” → Store shed nằm trên chính con đường rẽ phải đó (đi dọc theo đường này sẽ tới nơi). Câu chốt “If you come to the vegetable gardens, you've gone too far.” → Store shed nằm trước Vegetable Gardens . Trên bản đồ, vị trí thỏa điều kiện này đúng với điểm C → chọn C . 🧐 Lưu ý : ❌ D => Dễ nhầm vì cũng ở phía east/right khu Farm House, nhưng nếu đi tới gần Vegetable Gardens mới

passages.title: Stone Point: a New Zealand historical site
content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 3: "Stone Point: a New Zealand historical site"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [01:00] Liz: Hi Scott, here are my notes.
[01:04] Scott: Let's sort this presentation out then. The first thing I found out about Stone Point is it's an extinct volcanic cone. You probably know that already, being a New Zealander.
[01:12] Liz: Yes, and there are two other cones nearby, which also overlook the harbour.
[01:17] Scott: Right.

[01:18] Liz: Yeah, the first settlers of New Zealand, the Māori, sailed to New Zealand thousands of years after these volcanoes erupted. I think the tutor allocated us this topic though because of Stone Point's significant historical role. It's been used by both Māori and European settlers as a place to shelter from attack, or launch an attack, for centuries.
[01:41] Scott: Yeah, and the fact it was an ideal place for building a village, it would have been quite a sheltered spot.
[01:47] Liz: I suppose the Māori settled there because they thought the volcanic soil would help their crops grow.
[01:53] Scott: Well, they would have realised the benefits of the soil after a few good harvests, but initially the fishing opportunities would have been the attraction.
[02:00] Liz: You're right.
[02:02] Scott: Actually, I also read that Māori regard Stone Point as taonga. I believe that means a treasured thing.

[02:09] Liz: Wow, your Māori vocabulary is improving, Scott. Hmm, we do have to deal with Stone Point's cultural value for Māori. That's still part of its historical significance. But we need to keep most Māori terminology out of the presentation, otherwise a lot of the international students won't be able to follow us.

[02:30] Scott: That's a shame, I'm sure they'd be interested. I mean, I am. But yeah, we wouldn't be able to explain it in the time allowed, so I guess we have to stick to English. Anyway, European migrants turned Stone Point into a lookout point for ships, then it became a fort, an army base in the late 1880s, and then during the World Wars the fort was modernised again.
[02:53] Liz: It's also been a public park sometimes.
[02:56] Scott: I'd prefer to devote more of the presentation to the military use of Stone Point. There are some great websites about the engines they installed.

[03:04] Liz: Sorry, I wouldn't go into the technical side if I were you. If you start describing mechanical stuff, people will switch off. I think it's more interesting to look at the impact Stone Point had on the people's lives at the time. I mean, for example, there were about 25 years when they used local prisoners to build the tunnels and the underground rooms.
[03:28] Liz: They lived there too.
[03:30] Scott: Yeah, I guess, if we can find some first-hand accounts.

[04:22] Liz: OK, so let's make a checklist of things to do. For the Early Māori Inhabitation section, we have to look at the material we've used again and make sure we know who the writers were and when they wrote it.

[04:36] Scott: Yes, that needs work. And for the part about Stone Point being used as a lookout point, I'm sure we can locate some drawings of how Stone Point looked then and the kind of ships coming in.
[04:46] Liz: Nice. And what else? We haven't got a lot of detail for the reconstruction of the fort. We should add some more information about what it was the prisoners were adding to it.
[04:57] Scott: OK, I'll do that bit too.

[05:00] Liz: So I'll deal with the section regarding the modernisation that happened in the 1930s and 40s. I mean, that's the bit where we have the most visible evidence of historic buildings. I'll ring the Department of Conservation and see if they'll agree to let me film the site. Maybe allow me access to some of the tunnels the public don't see.
[05:21] Scott: OK. For the 1950s onwards, could you also arrange a meeting with someone from the Department of Conservation to ask them about their restoration work?
[05:30] Liz: I could try. Oh, and just about its use as a public park today. Where is the boundary exactly? Does it go all the way to the beach?
[05:39] Scott: Not sure. I'll check that out.
[05:41] Liz: Great. I suppose it would finish off the presentation nicely if we explain the future plans for the site.

questions.prompt: According to Liz, Stone Point played a key role in local history because
options: it was used for defence or attack purposes.
it was the landing point for the first Maori settlers.
it was developed as a commercial port.
questions.correct: it was used for defence or attack purposes.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "The first thing I found out about Stone Point is it's an extinct volcanic cone. You probably know that already, being a New Zealander. Yes, and there are two other cones nearby, which also overlook the harbour. Right. Yeah, the first settlers of New Zealand, the Māori, sailed to New Zealand thousands of years after these volcanoes erupted. I think the tutor allocated us this topic though because of Stone Point's significant historical role. It's "
explanation.step3: ❓ Câu hỏi : According to Liz, Stone Point played a key role in local history because ✅ Đáp án đúng : A. it was used for defence or attack purposes. ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : Đoạn Liz giải thích vì sao gia sư giao chủ đề này và nhắc đến vai trò lịch sử quan trọng của Stone Point: “because of Stone Point's significant historical role … ” ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi và gạch từ khóa: played a key role in local history + because → cần nghe lý do Stone Point quan trọng về mặt lịch sử. Trong bài nghe, Liz nói rõ tutor chọn chủ đề này vì vai trò lịch sử của Stone Point, rồi đưa lý do cụ thể: “shelter from attack” và “launch an attack” (= phòng thủ/trú ẩn hoặc tấn công ). Vì vậy, Stone Point quan trọng trong lịch sử địa phương vì từng được dùng cho
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: it was used for defence or attack purposes.

questions.prompt: Scott and Liz agree that Maori originally chose to inhabit Stone Point because of

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "I suppose the Māori settled there because they thought the volcanic soil would help their crops grow. Well, they would have realised the benefits of the soil after a few good harvests, but initially the fishing opportunities would have been the attraction. You're right."
explanation.step3: ❓ Câu hỏi : Scott and Liz agree that Maori originally chose to inhabit Stone Point because of ✅ Đáp án đúng : B. the supply of fish. ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : Đoạn Liz đưa ra lý do người Māori định cư và Scott sửa lại bằng “but initially…”: “I suppose the Māori settled there because…” / “but initially …” ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa: originally chose (= lý do ban đầu ) và agree (= hai người chốt cùng 1 ý ). Liz đoán: “volcanic soil would help their crops grow” (đất tốt cho trồng trọt) → đây là ý kiến ban đầu của Liz. Scott phản hồi bằng cấu trúc đối lập: “but initially the fishing opportunities would have been the attraction” → nhấn mạnh ban đầu họ bị thu hút bởi cơ hội đánh cá/nguồn cá . Liz kết luận: “You’re right.” → xá
explanation.step4: Đáp án chính xác: the supply of fish.

questions.prompt: Scott and Liz agree that using Maori terminology in their presentation
options: will be of interest to international students.
is required as a component of their research.

explanation.step1: Phân tích câu hỏi, xác định từ khóa và dự đoán thông tin theo Linearthinking.
explanation.step2: Trích dẫn bài đọc / Audio: "Actually, I also read that Māori regard Stone Point as taonga. I believe that means a treasured thing. Wow, your Māori vocabulary is improving, Scott. Hmm, we do have to deal with Stone Point's cultural value for Māori. That's still part of its historical significance. But we need to keep most Māori terminology out of the presentation, otherwise a lot of the international students won't be able to follow us. That's a shame, I'm sure they'd be int"

passages.title: Jatropha : a new biofuel
content: 📌 Jatropha : a new biofuel

Plant facts
The plant jatropha
- is originally from Central America
- can grow in poor [ _____ ]
- can survive [ _____ ] for several years
- can stop [ _____ ] of land

Its seeds
- can be used to produce diesel oil
- produce far more fuel than soybean or [ _____ ]
- leave a residue after processing-used to make electricity
- produce energy which is renewable. unlike fossil fuels

Uses of jatropha in Africa
- for water pumps and fridges
- made into [ _____ ]
- used as fencing
- the [ _____ ] are boiled and used to treat malaria
- for problems with [ _____ ]

European companies' claims about jatropha
- It could help stop poverty among rural populations
- It could be used in current diesel engines
- The plants use up lots of [ _____ ]

Problems with jatropha
- some seeds are toxic to people and animals
- unreliable oil productivity

Other criticisms of biofuels
- Widespread production of biofuels could result in
high food prices in poor countriesenvironmental damage caused by loss of rainforest and [ _____ ]adding to the problem of [ _____ ]
transcript: [01:11] AUDIO: Good afternoon. As you know, the world is running out of fossil fuels, that is, crude oil, coal and natural gas. As an alternative, certain plants are now being considered as biofuels, which are fuels made from organic plant material. These are possible sources of energy once the fossil fuels have gone forever.

[01:33] AUDIO: Well, one such plant goes by the name of Jatropha. It was first a native of Central America and it's now found across the world. A few things that make this plant especially attractive is that it can survive in very poor quality infertile soil, as it does, for example, alongside train tracks in India on the line between Mumbai and Delhi. And for up to three years it's resistant to drought.

[01:59] AUDIO: That's right, it can do without rain for that long. And even if it's not actually a plant that people can eat, it's still worth having it on your land as it prevents erosion. And we looked at the dangerous consequences of that in a previous lecture. Furthermore, Jatropha seeds can be slowly distilled to produce diesel oil, and it's this kind of fuel, of course, that's of interest to scientists and power companies.

[02:24] AUDIO: After processing, the seeds can yield up to four times the oil that soybean can, and ten times the amount compared to corn. So you can see why it's causing such interest. And not much is wasted in the processing procedure either. After the oil has been extracted from the seeds, the residue is processed into biomass which can run power stations, which in turn can provide electricity for thousands of local homes.

[02:52] AUDIO: Also, whereas our fossil fuels cannot be replaced, the energy produced by biofuels such as Jatropha is renewable. It's not going to run out because the plants just go on growing. There's no doubt that it is a remarkable plant, and one that has been very beneficial to man. In various African communities, it's been used to operate water pumps and refrigerate medicines.

[03:21] AUDIO: It can be used to produce candles, or as a fencing plant to keep some animals enclosed, and some animals out. It can also treat a number of health problems. For example, the boiled leaves can do much to relieve the suffering of people with malaria. And some Jatropha species have seeds which are used to treat digestion problems.

[03:44] AUDIO: Anyway, that's not what the European corporations who are buying vast amounts of land for Jatropha plantations are focusing on. They claim that people who are dependent on rural economies will benefit from growing Jatropha, and that it will help them bring an end to poverty by providing a long-term local industry. They also point out that few or no modifications would be necessary in modern diesel engines since they were originally designed to run on biofuels such as peanut oil and ethanol anyway. Of course, when the plants are burnt, they release carbon dioxide, but they absorb great amounts when they're growing, making them a considerably greener alternative to fossil fuels.

[04:27] AUDIO: But not everyone shares the excitement over Jatropha, nor other biofuels. In Western Australia, Jatropha has in fact been banned since the seeds of some species are toxic, and it only takes three or four to kill a person. And animals are also very vulnerable. Furthermore, sceptics also point out that as there are many species of Jatropha, its oil productivity is unreliable.

[04:53] AUDIO: Aside from this, critics of Jatropha and other biofuels claim that farmers now have a strong economic incentive to grow them rather than food crops. Poor countries would be particularly affected because they would have to rely on imported foods to survive, and people would end up having to pay greatly inflated prices for basic foods. There's also the concern over environmental damage. In order to provide land for palm oil or sugarcane plantations, for instance, companies are cutting down vast areas of rainforest which can never be replaced, and this in turn results in the disappearance of wildlife which depended on that habitat.

[05:36] AUDIO: You can also imagine that such deforestation makes a considerable contribution to global warming. Furthermore, opponents also reject the idea that biofuels are a carbon-neutral source of energy.

Dự đoán thông tin cần điền là một vấn đề môi trường mà phá rừng gây ra. ✅ Đáp án đúng : global warming ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : đoạn người nói nhắc đến việc các công ty chặt phá những khu vực rừng mưa rộng lớn (rainforest) để làm đồn điền (plantations) và nói về hậu quả môi trường . ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi, chốt từ khóa: adding + problem (thêm vào vấn đề…). passages.title: A Residence Survey
content: 📌 A Residence Survey

Current occupation: [ _____ ]
Length of living in the north: [ _____ ]
Exact living area: [ _____ ]
Type of accommodation: a shared [ _____ ]
Means of transport:
- Private: walking and bicycles
- Public: [ _____ ] and taxi

Frequency of eating out: [ _____ ]
Places for entertainment: [ _____ ]
Other free time activity: go to the [ _____ ]
Preferred exercises:

go swimminggo to the gymgo [ _____ ]
Parttime course: [ _____ ]
transcript: [01:42] Woman: Excuse me?
[01:43] Lee: Yes?
[01:44] Woman: I was wondering if you could spare a few minutes to do a questionnaire on your residency here in the north. It won't take long.
[01:51] Lee: No, that's fine.
[01:52] Woman: Lovely. First of all, may I get some information about yourself?
[01:57] Woman: May I know your name and age?
[02:00] Lee: My name's Lee and I'm 19 years old now.
[02:04] Woman: Great. And could I ask what your job is? Are you a student?
[02:08] Lee: Actually, I'm going to continue my study in business management next month, but at the moment I'm a salesman by profession.
[02:17] Woman: Oh, right. And how long have you been living here in the north?

[02:21] Lee: Well, I have been in this city since I was three years old, but my family and I had lived in the east for seven years at first. Now I am 19, so I have spent about nine years living here till now.
[02:34] Woman: Great. Which part of the northern area do you live in?
[02:38] Lee: I live in Spring Park. Have you heard of it?
[02:41] Woman: Yes, of course. So what about your accommodation? Do you live in a house or a flat or something similar?
[02:48] Lee: I used to live with my family in a big house, and now I'm living in an apartment with two of my friends, who are my colleagues as well.
[02:57] Woman: Oh, right. And one more question. What means of transport will you take when you need to go somewhere?

[03:05] Lee: If it's not too far away, I'd prefer to go on foot or by bicycle. If there is a long way to go, I take the train or sometimes a cab. I rarely take buses, because I think the most important things to keep in mind are time and comfort.
[03:23] Woman: Great. Thanks. Now, let's go to the second part of my questionnaire. I'd like you to tell me, how often do you dine out? Is it once a week or several times a year?
[04:12] Lee: I'm afraid neither of those options agree with me. I don't often go out for dinner, maybe once a month. Every week just seems too often for me.
[04:22] Woman: OK, then where do you usually go for recreation?
[04:26] Lee: I often go to places that other people go to. I sometimes go clubbing after work. You know, there are some fantastic clubs nearby.
[04:35] Woman: And if you do not have to work during the day, will you go for a show or something?

[04:40] Lee: You know, there is the newly built theatre that opened last month in Spring Park, but I rarely go there because it's too expensive. I prefer to go to the cinema to see some of the latest movies.
[04:52] Woman: Do you like doing sports? And what is your main form of exercise?
[04:57] Lee: I like swimming and I go to the gym occasionally, but I spend most of my spare time sailing.
[05:04] Woman: All right. Last question. Have you taken any part-time courses?
[05:10] Lee: Yes, because I'm really keen on cartoons. I'm doing a Japanese course during the weekends, but I'm still a beginner.
[05:18] Woman: Wow, what a special language. Most people I know would like to learn Spanish or Latin. You must be brilliant. Well, thank you very much for your time.
[05:28] Lee: No problem. Bye.

explanation.step3: ❓ Câu hỏi : Current occupation: _______ 🎯 Xác định loại từ cần điền : Sau Current occupation cần điền một danh từ chỉ nghề nghiệp hiện tại . ✅ Đáp án đúng : salemans ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : câu hỏi của người phụ nữ về job: "what your job is?" và câu tiếp theo “Are you a student?” ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi và xác định từ khóa cần bắt: Current occupation (nghề nghiệp hiện tại). Khi nghe, Lee nói: “I’m going to continue my study…” → đây là kế hoạch học tập trong tương lai , chưa phải nghề hiện tại. Ngay sau đó có cụm quan trọng “but at the moment” → báo hiệu thông tin đúng về hiện tại sẽ xuất hiện. Lee chốt lại: “I’m a salesman by profession” → salesman chính là nghề của Lee. 🧐 Lưu ý : ❌ student => người hỏi nhắc “ Are you a student? ”

Thông tin cần nghe là tổng thời gian sống ở khu vực phía bắc (in the north). ✅ Đáp án đúng : 9 years ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : câu hỏi của người phụ nữ về thời gian bạn ấy đã sống ở phía bắc (“And how long have you been living here in the north?”). ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi và khoanh vùng từ khóa Length + living in the north ⇒ chắc chắn đáp án là quãng thời gian . Khi nghe, chú ý người nói có thể nhắc nơi từng sống trước đây để gây nhiễu. Trong bài nghe, Lee nói: đã ở thành phố này từ 3 tuổi , nhưng ban đầu gia đình sống ở miền đông 7 năm . Nội dung cần nghe là khu vực sinh sống trong northern area ⇒ dự đoán là tên quận/khu/park/area . ✅ Đáp án đúng : Spring Park ▶️ Bắt đầu nghe ở : câu hỏi “Which part of the northern area do you live in?” (người phụ nữ hỏi về khu vực Lee đang sống ). ☺️ Giải thích đáp án : Đọc câu hỏi và khoanh vùng từ khóa Exact living area để biết mình cần nghe tên địa danh . content: 🎧 HƯỚNG DẪN NGHE PART 2: "Group Project"

Bấm nút Play trên trình phát Audio phía trên để nghe bài thu âm chuẩn quốc tế và hoàn thành các câu hỏi ở cột bên phải. Bạn có thể chuyển sang tab "Transcript Hội Thoại" để đối chiếu lời thoại chi tiết và bấm giờ từng câu.
transcript: [00:52] AUDIO: Welcome everyone to this farmers and growers market in the quiet village of Havelock North. My name is Helen and I'm your guide for the morning. Before I let you go off and explore, I'll just tell you a few things first which will help you know both what sort of products you will find here, there's everything from fresh produce to handcrafts, and then how to find your way around. Right, so what do people sell here?

[01:23] AUDIO: Well, for a start, there's some very nice hand cream from the far north, which is always a top seller abroad. Those of you visitors who come from other countries may like to take it back home with you as presents because the packaging is branded New Zealand and has pretty pictures on it of our native flowers. Now there's also some very tasty jam available, although because it's made from blueberries, this product is quite dear, so you'll have to spend a little more than usual. Still, very delicious though.

[02:00] AUDIO: And for those of you who like your bath products gentle and suitable for sensitive skin, there are some non-allergenic soaps here, not perfumed or coloured, just simple soap, through and through, made by hand the old-fashioned way with nothing artificial added. Ah, now there are the candles for sale at a very reasonable price. They probably represent the top buy if you want your dollar to stretch as far as possible. They're just the colour of wax so that's not too exciting, but they do come in all different sizes to suit different purposes.

[02:38] AUDIO: Um, just a couple more items for me to tell you about. There's great flavoured ice cream on offer. In fact, it's so good that it's classified export grade and was awarded the gold medal at this year's food fair. You should try some.

[02:55] AUDIO: And finally, we've got shampoo, which comes in cute little blue, green and red bottles for three different hair types. The best thing about this product is that it's produced right here in Havelock North Village by a farmer's wife who started her own company. Right, so that's given you an idea of the sorts of products which are on sale at this market. Now, let's just give you a quick rundown on where to find everything, then I'll let you go for a walk around to do your shopping.

[04:03] AUDIO: As you enter the market, through the gate here in front of us, at the bottom of the map you've been given, you'll see immediately that the farmers have set up their stalls out in a square in the middle of the vineyard. I know a few of you are interested in buying wooden handicrafts, so just to let you know that the stall is located on the far side of the walking track opposite the entrance. There are some lovely toys for sale there, and also hand-carved wooden platters and bowls. Now the first one you'd see to your left after entering, tucked away there by the gate, is the china store, where there's an interesting display of old, second-hand or antique teacups and saucers.

[04:52] AUDIO: What else? Oh yes, the wool shop. For those of you who are wanting to take home a New Zealand sheepskin rug or a woolly jersey for the winter, can be found on your immediate right after you've gone in the entrance. There are some nice scarves and hats there too.

[05:10] AUDIO: Now after all this shopping you'll be needing a drink and something to eat, so go into the circular stand in the middle and you'll find a stall selling local wine, fruit juices and cordials. And that's the one at the centre top, furthest away from the main gate, and also a stall with lots of snack food to keep you going. Well that's all from me folks, now enjoy the market.

Câu sau củng cố: “you'll have to spend a little more than usual” → phải trả nhiều tiền hơn bình thường ⇒ chọn expensive . 🧐 Lưu ý : ❌ D => Dễ nhầm nếu chỉ nhớ phần “tasty/delicious” và nghĩ là “đáng tiền”, nhưng audio nói rõ dear và spend a little more (giá cao), không phải best value . ❌ H => là cho ice cream (được gold medal ), không phải jam . ❌ G => là cho hand cream (top seller abroad), không liên quan jam .

passages.title: Taking part in archaeological excavations
content: 📌 Choose FIVE correct letters from A-I.
transcript: [01:05] May: Hi Thomas. Did you have a good time in Turkey?

[01:09] Thomas: Hi May. I had a great time. But I have to say, although I've always been keen on being an archaeologist, before I went on an excavation, I used to find some of the things we did in class totally mystifying.
[01:23] May: Me too. Before I did my trip to Egypt, I was often irritated at not being able to picture exactly what the lecturers meant. They were always so excited about everything.
[01:36] Thomas: Yeah. We did a lot of practical stuff on the excavation, which I really needed. Was it harder than you expected?
[01:44] AUDIO: <v May? Yes, mostly.

[01:45] May: I learned a lot more about the rules of archaeology. I was really taken aback by how precise you have to be with your data collection and recording. I took loads of photographs and they proved very useful, and the drawing went well too.

[02:01] Thomas: Yes, I think I'm quite good with the camera. I'm minded about the recording though. I had no idea it would take so much time. Did you find anything particularly interesting when you were digging?

[02:13] May: I did, actually. I had to dig a trench in part of the site. Interestingly, there weren't any bits of pottery there like you would expect to find, but I did get out some pieces of cloth and what looked like one or two silver beads. But our team leader said that they weren't.
[02:31] May: They were probably lead weights for weaving. What about you?

[02:36] Thomas: I didn't find anything myself, but quite a few of the other students did. What I enjoyed was trying to identify what crops the people who had once lived in the area had grown. They seemed to have had a much better diet than I expected. Fish and wheat as well as oats, honey and fruit.
[02:54] Thomas: Lots of different things.

[02:56] May: Yes, it's amazing, isn't it? And from measuring the bones in one of the sites, we found that the people were actually taller and had better teeth than the people who live in the area today.
[03:08] Thomas: Probably due to less carbohydrates. How were the people you had to work with? My team was great. They were made up of people my age from all over the world.
[03:19] Thomas: It was good to work with them. Lots of fun and they taught me a lot. It was tough for us all, though, getting up at dawn every day and being out until late afternoon.
[03:31] May: Oh, that's true enough. ? We were all exhausted. And I'd like to have an international team next time. Mine was mainly made up of English and Americans.
[03:42] May: I enjoyed the field school, but everyone was much more experienced and older than I was. It was a bit scary.
[04:03] Thomas: You know there's going to be a question about the excavation projects in our test next week. Should we just run through it for practice?

[04:11] May: Good idea. Our team leader was very strict about following the right procedure. He used to say, never excavate anything if you're not sure it's worth excavating. Now I think that when you've decided where to excavate, you go to the site hut and get whatever tools you need.
[04:30] May: Then clean the area so you know exactly how big it's going to be.
[04:35] Thomas: Right.
[04:35] May: Okay. And you need to make sure you can remember what the site looks like before you begin digging.
[04:42] Thomas: I think photos are probably best for that, rather than drawings at this stage.

[04:47] May: I agree. You then attach them to a record sheet, which you get from the team leader, remembering to put in the site code, unit number, and time. So much red tape. You seem to spend half the time marking rather than digging.
[05:03] Thomas: That's true. I think you then have to draw up a detailed plan of where you're digging, and then measure the limits.

[05:10] May: And this is all before you actually start digging. Okay, so far so good. Now you can start with the trowel, but first you have to get soil samples, and you keep them for further analysis. Anything that you don't think is useful, you leave in place on the site.
[05:29] Thomas: Yes, and if you make any finds, that is, any object you retrieve, including animal bone, stone, as well as artifacts, they should all be registered and labeled.
[05:40] May: And then you put them in a plastic bag and return them to the site hut.
[05:45] Thomas: That's right, and remember to leave the tools and site hut as you would expect to find them.
[05:52] May: Looks like we've learned something after all.

passages.title: Crocodile Study
content: 📌 Crocodile Study

Background
- Type of crocodile studied: crocodiles found in salt water
- Location of study: Northern Territory, Australia
- Significance of study: unique because it was the first time a [ _____ ] had been used to track crocodiles

Previous studies:
- done using [ _____ ] 
- stressful method, also unreliable due to loss of the [ _____ ] 
Reasons for study: the management of crocodiles by the government may not be effective

Research questions:
- How far can crocodiles travel?
- How easily can crocodiles [ _____ ] ?
Challenge: crocodiles are difficult to observe because they avoid [ _____ ]

Details of study:
- number of crocodiles involved: three
- method: crocodiles were measured and tagged then relocated using a [ _____ ] 
- monitoring: scientists got data from a transmitter located on the crocodile's [ _____ ]

Results of study:
- Each crocodile
- first stayed at the site for a few weeks, moving in a random way
- then took the most [ _____ ] way home

Conclusions:
- a change in policy is needed
- when travelling long distances, crocodiles may use
i. their own senses and the position of the [ _____ ] 
ii. a similar system to [ _____ ]
transcript: [01:17] AUDIO: Hello everybody. I've just arrived back from my field trip, and Professor Martin has asked me to tell you about it today in our research forum. As many of you know already, my dissertation relates to crocodile behavior. My specialty is the saltwater crocodile, which is much larger than the freshwater crocodile.

[01:37] AUDIO: I've just come back from the Northern Territory, where I've been part of a groundbreaking study observing crocodile movements. Ah, it's not the only time crocodile movements have been followed, but this study is unique because we tracked crocodiles using a satellite. Up until now, studies like this one have only been able to track crocodile movements using radio. Not only was this method more stressful for the animal, which had to be caught several times, but it was also not very reliable, as the signal was often lost.

[02:11] AUDIO: So you might be wondering why we chose to track crocodiles. Well, crocodile attacks on people and livestock are rare, but when they do happen, the government believes that the problem crocodile should be relocated, rather than killed. But can we be sure that the crocodile won't simply return to the place where it came from? So we designed a study to try to answer these questions.

[02:35] AUDIO: We wanted to establish, firstly, how far crocodiles can travel over a period of time. The second thing that we wanted to know was how easy is it for crocodiles to navigate? Could they find their own way home again if they were moved to another location? Of course, the biggest challenge when observing crocodiles is that they are very secretive animals.

[02:58] AUDIO: They stay well away from people if they can, which makes them really difficult to follow. I'll give you some information about the design of the study now. There were three crocodiles in our study, all from the Northern Territory, and measuring between three and four and a half meters in length. The crocodiles were captured, measured and tagged, and then taken by helicopter to new locations up to 400 kilometers away from where they were found.

[03:32] AUDIO: We were then able to use the tracking data to monitor their movements. We used a specially designed transmitter, which we attached to each animal's head. The transmitter collected the data and relayed it back to us. The results of our study were quite astounding.

[03:48] AUDIO: After they were released, each crocodile remained in the release site for some weeks, making random movements around the site each day. But then they each swam home, traveling by the most direct route. These crocodiles showed remarkable navigational skills and stamina to swim such long voyages. So what conclusions did we draw from this?

[04:11] AUDIO: Well, we proved that crocodiles are clearly capable of making marathon swims to find their way home. This meant that the current policy should be reconsidered. You might be wondering how the crocodiles managed to get home. We concluded that they used factors such as sight and smell, as well as their position to the sun, to point their way.

[04:33] AUDIO: It's a little-known fact that crocodiles are more closely related to birds than they are to any other reptile, so we believe it's possible that they used the same system to negotiate long journeys. Now that the study has been completed, let's take a look at the results of our study.
